data.name: Acoustic Guitar
data.description: A playable acoustic guitar used to attract ARC's attention and impress other Raiders.
data.article:
The Acoustic Guitar is an instrument used to play melodies, which can attract nearby ARCs. Other Raiders can also play along with instruments such as the Recorder or Shaker. While playing, actions that require both hands are not possible.

  • It can be purchased from Shani for 70 coins, with a limit of one per day.
  • One is obtained upon completing the project Trophy Display.
  • It is also found on page 3 of Decks: Raider Deck AR/RD 002: Goalie.

data.name: Adrenaline Shot
data.description: A serum that fully restores stamina and temporarily increases stamina regeneration
data.article:
The Adrenaline Shot is a quick-use item that completely restores your stamina and temporarily makes it regenerate faster. This helps you keep moving or use stamina-draining abilities more often when you need to.

These shots can be found by scavenging in the environment, crafted at a Medical Lab or with the In-Round Crafting skill, or purchased from Lance for 900 coins.

data.name: Advanced ARC Powercell
data.description: Very valuable resource that drops from certain ARC enemies
data.article:
The Advanced ARC Powercell is a resource item scavenged from ARCs like the Bastion, Courier, and Sentinel.

It is used in crafting various supplies at Workbench and Medical Lab. This item can also be recycled to gain other resources.

data.name: Advanced Electrical Components
data.description: Used to craft a wide range of items. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.flavor_text: Used to craft: Tactical Mk. 3 (Defensive), Combat Mk. 3 (Flanking), Combat Mk. 3 (Aggressive), Looting Mk. 3 (Cautious), Tactical Mk. 3 (Healing)
data.article:
Advanced Electrical Components are a refined material primarily used to craft various items and to upgrade your Hideout.

You can acquire these components by scavenging them from the environment or by looting arcs. They can also be crafted at the Refiner.

data.name: Advanced Mechanical Components
data.description: Mostly used to craft advanced weapons. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article:
Advanced Mechanical Components are a refined material primarily used for crafting and upgrading items. They support your weapon crafting at the Gunsmith in your Hideout, enabling the creation of various advanced weapons and high-end components.

  • You can find this item by defeating specific ARCs such as the Queen.
  • It can also be looted from various containers or environmental spots during your raids.
  • Another way is to craft it yourself at a Refiner using other materials.

This item can be recycled for resources.

data.name: Agave
data.description: A piece of an agave leaf. Can be used to regain a small amount of health.
data.article: Agave is an uncommon healing item that helps Raiders regain a small amount of health over time when consumed. It can be found by harvesting agave plants in the Dam Battlegrounds map and the outskirts of the Buried City map. Raiders can also scavenge for it inside wicker baskets. This item can also be used to craft healing supplies.

data.name: Agave Juice
data.description: A concoction that temporarily increases stamina regeneration, at a small initial cost to health.
data.article: Agave Juice is a consumable item that Raiders can use to temporarily increase their stamina regeneration, while taking a small amount of health damage at the start. This helps Raiders quickly regain stamina during raids and it can only be crafted in-raid.

data.name: Air Freshener
data.description: May be worth a few coins.
data.article: The Air Freshener is a trinket that Raiders collect. Its primary role is to be sold for coins, offering a simple way to earn funds during your raids. This item also has a secondary use as a crafting component: it can be combined with other materials to create crafted items, a process that takes place directly during an active raid. You can obtain it by thoroughly searching the environment and looting various containers.

data.name: Alarm Clock
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Alarm Clock is a resource Raiders can find by searching and looting within residential areas throughout the various maps. Its main use is to be recycled for basic crafting materials, which are helpful for crafting new gear or upgrading existing items at a crafting workbench in your Hideout.

data.name: Alien Duck
data.description: A long, long way from home.
data.flavor_text: Can be thrown to create noise.
data.article: The Alien Duck is a decorative item, a variant of the Rubber Duck. It serves to personalize your Raider Den in your Hideout, or you can throw it to create noise, which can be used as a distraction. You can obtain this item by scavenging inside chimneys when the "Bird City" event is active. Other similar collectible duck variants include the Doodly Duck, Familiar Duck, Flashy Duck, Gentle Duck, and Tropical Duck.

data.name: Ancient Fort Security Code
data.description: Temporary security code to unlock the main gate.
data.flavor_text: Can only be used during Locked Gate
data.article: The Ancient Fort Security Code is a temporary code used to unlock a main gate within the Ancient Fort area during the 'Locked Gate' map condition. You need four of these codes to open the gate. Find this item in lootable containers located in the Ancient Fort area of the Blue Gate map. To use a code, go to the Gate Control Room on the Blue Gate map, enter the building, and submit it at one of the four terminals. Submitting a code consumes it and activates the terminal which helps to open the Locked Gate.

data.name: Angled Grip I
data.description: Slightly reduces horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Arpeggio, II toro, Venator, Bobcat, Tempest, Vulcano

data.article: The Angled Grip I is a weapon modification designed to improve how steadily you can hold your weapon while aiming. It helps reduce horizontal recoil, making it easier to control your shots. Weapon modifications, including grips, can be found by searching through various containers during raids, or they can be crafted at the appropriate station.

data.name: Angled Grip II
data.description: Moderately reduces horizontal recoil.
data.article: The Angled Grip II is a weapon attachment that helps reduce the sideways kick of your weapon when you shoot. You can obtain this grip by crafting it at the Gunsmith once you have the Angled Grip II Blueprint. The blueprint can be found by searching various containers or purchased from the vendor Shani for 100 coins, with a limit of two per day.

data.name: Angled Grip II Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Angled Grip II
data.article: The Angled Grip II Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Angled Grip II weapon modification at a Gunsmith workbench, which helps reduce a weapon's horizontal recoil. Once you learn it by using it in Speranza, you can craft the modification. Raiders can obtain this blueprint by scavenging residential containers found across all maps. It is also available as a reward from Weekly Trials or can be purchased from the vendor Shani for coins.

data.name: Angled Grip III
data.description: Significantly reduces horizontal recoil.

stat_block.compatibleWeapons: Ferro, Kettle, Rattler, Stitcher, Arpeggio, II toro, Venator, Bettina, Bobcat, Tempest, Vulcano, Aphelion

data.flavor_text: 40% Reduced Horizontal Recoil - 30% Reduced ADS Speed
data.article: The Angled Grip III is a weapon modification designed to improve your shooting accuracy by significantly reducing your weapon's sideways movement during firing. You can craft it at a Gunsmith Bench level 1 using the Angled Grip III blueprint. Keeping track of blueprints is easier with the Needed Items Tracker. Another way to obtain it is by purchasing it directly from the vendor Tian Wen for 15,000 coins, although he only has one available for sale each day. Once you have it, it can be recycled for general resources.

data.name: Angled Grip III Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Angled Grip III
data.article: The Angled Grip III Blueprint is a blueprint that unlocks the crafting recipe for the Angled Grip III at a Workbench. You can find this blueprint by scavenging inside Residential Containers across any map. It appears specifically during certain map conditions, like an Electromagnetic Storm, Locked Gate, or Night Raid. Alternatively, it can be acquired as a reward from Weekly Trials.

data.name: Antiseptic
data.description: Used to craft medical supplies. Can be recycled into chemicals.
data.article:
Antiseptic is a refined material used to craft medical supplies and upgrading facilities. It is also essential for upgrading your Medical Lab within your Hideout.

Raiders mainly acquire Antiseptic by crafting it at the Refiner. Additionally, it can be found by scavenging the environment and searching containers in medical areas across the map.

data.name: Anvil Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Anvil - Has high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
data.article:
The Anvil Blueprint is a blueprint that allows you to craft the Anvil I hand cannon. Once you have it, this blueprint also allows you to upgrade it into its improved versions: Anvil II, Anvil III, and Anvil IV. Crafting requires access to a Gunsmith station found in your Hideout.

You can find the Anvil Blueprint by opening Raider Caches and other various containers or you can purchase the weapon itself from Tian Wen for coins.

data.name: Anvil I
data.description: Single-action hand cannon with high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
data.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating.
data.article: The Anvil I is a hand cannon that uses ammunition. It is effective for hitting targets at medium range, providing strong damage and high headshot damage, though it has a slow firing speed. Raiders can find it by scavenging in the environment or craft it at a Gunsmith after learning the Anvil Blueprint. It can also be purchased from Tian Wen for coins.

data.name: Anvil II
data.description: Single-action hand cannon with high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
data.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating.
data.article: The Anvil II is an improved version of the Anvil I hand cannon, which delivers high damage, especially with headshots, and is effective at medium range. It uses heavy ammo. This upgraded version offers a faster firing rate and increased durability compared to its base model, making it more effective in combat. You can craft it at the Gunsmith using an existing Anvil I.

data.name: Anvil III
data.description: Single-action hand cannon with high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
data.flavor_text: Very effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Anvil III is an upgraded hand cannon that improves upon the Anvil II model. It uses heavy ammo and is designed for high damage, particularly with headshots at medium range. While it maintains a slow handling speed, this version boasts a 50% increased fire rate and better shot accuracy, making it more effective in combat. Raiders obtain it by upgrading an Anvil II at the Gunsmith.

data.name: Anvil IV
data.description: Single-action hand cannon with high damage output and headshot damage, but slow handling.
data.article: The Anvil IV is the most advanced version of the Anvil hand cannon, firing ammunition. It is designed for hitting targets at medium range and delivers high damage, especially with headshots. Compared to earlier versions, it fires faster and recovers its accuracy more quickly after shooting. This hand cannon is acquired by upgrading an Anvil III at the Gunsmith. To begin crafting the line, you first need to find an Anvil Blueprint, which can be looted from containers.

data.name: Anvil Splitter
data.description: Compatible with: Anvil  - Tech mod for the Anvil that replaces its bullets with ones that split into 4 weaker projectiles.
data.article: The Anvil Splitter is a weapon modification designed for the Anvil gun. Its primary role is to change how it fires, making each shot split into four separate projectiles instead of one. While each of these individual split projectiles deals less damage, this mod significantly increases the overall number of projectiles released with every shot. This item can be obtained through scavenging, typically found while exploring different areas.

data.name: Aphelion Rifle
data.description: Fires high velocity energy rounds.
data.article:
The Aphelion is a two-round-burst Battle Rifle designed for fighting ARCs. It fires energy rounds and uses ammunition.

To obtain the Aphelion, you first need to acquire its blueprint, which can be found in the Stella Montis map. Once you have it, it can be crafted at a Gunsmith. Additionally, it may be earned as a reward for completing the Furtive Meetings quest.

data.name: Aphelion Rifle Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft an Aphelion Rifle
data.article: This blueprint allows Raiders to craft the Aphelion Rifle at a Workbench, provided they have achieved the required Gunsmith bench level. It is known for firing high-velocity energy rounds in two-round bursts. You can find it pretty commonly in the Stella Montis map.

data.name: Apricot
data.description: A sun ripe apricot. Can be consumed for a small amount of stamina.
data.article:
The Apricot is an uncommon fruit that gives you a small boost of stamina when consumed. It also plays a role in training your Scrappy companion.

You can find Apricots by harvesting them directly from Apricot trees, which are recognized by their green and yellow leaves and small size. When you interact with a tree, it can drop several Apricots. They also commonly spawn on the ground beneath these trees. Additionally, you might discover them by scavenging inside wicker baskets. They are often found on the Blue Gate map.

data.name: Arcade Duck
data.description: Can be thrown to create noise.

data.name: ARC Alloy
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities, or by recycling certain ARC parts. Used to craft components.
data.article:
ARC Alloy is a versatile material essential for crafting various components and useful items, helping Raiders advance their gear and complete important projects.

Raiders primarily obtain ARC Alloy by looting arcs and scavenging their remains. It can also be acquired by recycling salvage. Once obtained, it is used at crafting stations to create items. It is also required for progressing through different project stages in your Hideout.

data.name: ARC Circuitry
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Used to craft components. Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
data.article: ARC Circuitry is a rare component essential for crafting and repairing gear. You can obtain it by defeating various ARCs such as the Baron Husk, Bastion, Courier, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Rocketeer, and Surveyor. It can also be crafted at the Refiner or salvaged from items.

data.name: ARC Coolant
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Can be recycled into chemicals
data.article: ARC Coolant is a resource found by salvaging defeated ARCs. It is a specific type of coolant, different from Impure ARC Coolant or standard Coolant. You can obtain it by defeating various ARCs such as the Comet, Fireball, Matriarch, Pop, Queen, Sentinel, Surveyor, and Vaporizer.

data.name: ARC Flex Rubber
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Can be recycled into rubber.
data.article: ARC Flex Rubber is a rare material that Raiders can recycle to obtain crafting resources. It is obtained by defeating various ARCs across different maps.

data.name: ARC Motion Core
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Used to craft components. Can be recycled into ARC Alloy.
data.article:
The ARC Motion Core is a rare item used to craft various components and upgrade your facilities. It is essential for upgrading your Refiner.

You can get ARC Motion Cores through these methods:

  • By defeating various Bastion, Courier, Leaper, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Rocketeer, Sentinel, Surveyor, and Turbine.

  • By crafting it at the Refiner.

data.name: ARC Performance Steel
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Can be recycled into scrap metal.
data.article: ARC Performance Steel is a component used for crafting various items and progressing in certain Expedition Projects. It is obtained by defeating various ARCs found across different maps. Common sources include ARCs such as Arc Probe, Arc Husk, Baron Husk, and Arc Courier. These are frequently encountered in the Blue Gate map, the Dam Battlegrounds map, and the Spaceport map. Additionally, it can be acquired during specific world events like Electromagnetic Storms or Husk Graveyards. This item can also be recycled for resources.

data.name: ARC Powercell
data.description: Valuable resource that drops from all ARC enemies. Used to craft: Shield Recharger
data.article: The ARC Powercell is a common resource used to repair your shields during raids. Using an ARC Powercell restores 20 shield charge over 10 seconds. You can obtain these by defeating any ARCs you encounter, or by scavenging through containers found around the various maps. Additionally, it can be crafted at Workbench, Medical Lab, or by using the In-Round Crafting skill.

data.name: ARC Synthetic Resin
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies or activities. Can be recycled into plastic.
data.article: ARC Synthetic Resin is a valuable crafting material that helps you complete various projects, such as the Trophy Display project. You can track your progress on projects like this using the Needed Items Tracker. This item is obtained by salvaging it from defeated ARCs. Many different types of ARCs are known to drop this material, including the Baron Husk, Deforester Husk, Hornet, Matriarch, Probe, Queen, Sentinel, Shredder, Snitch, Spotter, Turbine, Turret, and Wasp.

data.name: ARC Thermo Lining
data.description: Obtained from ARC enemies and activities. Can be recycled into fabric.
data.article: ARC Thermo Lining is a material you get from looting arcs. Its main use is to be recycled, which provides valuable crafting resources for your projects. You can obtain it by defeating many different kinds of ARCs, including smaller ones like the Wasp, Tick, Pop, or Fireball, and larger ones such as the Sentinel and Matriarch. But the most reliable way to get this material is to loot Baron Husks and Landing ARC Probes.

data.name: Arpeggio I
data.description: Has decent damage output and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Arpeggio I is an assault rifle that fires in three-round bursts and uses Medium Ammo. It is a balanced weapon with good damage output and accuracy. This weapon can be acquired by finding it while scavenging, or it can be crafted at a Hideout crafting bench with Gunsmith. It serves as the base version, which can be upgraded to the Arpeggio II, then Arpeggio III, and finally the Arpeggio IV. If you no longer need it, the item can be recycled for resources or sold for 5,500 coins.

data.name: Arpeggio II
data.description: A 3-round burst assault rifle with decent damage output and accuracy.
data.flavor_text: Somewhat effective against ARC armor plating
data.article: The Arpeggio II is an upgraded version of the Arpeggio I assault rifle, providing improved combat performance. It fires in three-round bursts and uses Medium Ammo. This upgraded rifle offers a faster firing rate, quicker reloads, and increased durability. Raiders can obtain it by crafting at a Gunsmith workbench in their Hideout. It can also sometimes be found through scavenging while exploring different maps. Like other items, it can be recycled for resources or sold for coins.

data.name: Arpeggio III
data.description: A 3-round burst assault rifle with decent damage output and accuracy.
data.article: The Arpeggio III is an upgraded three-round-burst assault rifle that offers improved combat performance. It uses medium ammo. This rifle provides a faster fire rate, quicker reloads, and increased durability compared to its previous version, the Arpeggio II. Raiders obtain it by crafting at the Gunsmith.

data.name: Arpeggio IV
data.description: A 3-round burst assault rifle with decent damage output and accuracy.
data.article: The Arpeggio IV is an advanced assault rifle that fires in three-round bursts and uses medium ammo. It helps Raiders in combat against ARCs by providing a higher fire rate, faster reloading, and better durability compared to its earlier versions. This weapon is crafted from an Arpeggio III at a Gunsmith. Raiders can also sell it for coins or recycle it for salvage.

data.name: Assessor Matrix
data.description: Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: Assessor Matrix is a specialized part obtained by breaching the ARC Assessor. This unique ARC, a recent arrival, descends from orbit and, guided by ARC Surveyors, lands in pre-set places on the map spawning a patrol of flying ARC enemies around it. The ARC Assessor appears during the Close Scrutiny event.

data.name: Assorted Seeds
data.description: A handful of seeds. Celeste might be looking for these.
data.article: Assorted Seeds are resources Raiders can collect and spend. Their main use is to acquire rare items through trade, offering a way to obtain goods that are not typically found during regular raids in the various maps.

data.name: Aviator (Outfit)
data.description: Aviator outfit is a quest reward from Armored Transports.
data.article: The Aviator (Outfit) is an outfit used to customize your character's appearance in the game. Raiders can obtain this outfit by successfully completing a specific raid. Please note that the exact raid required to unlock it has changed over time.

data.name: Bag (Radio Renegade Variant)
data.description: Radio Renegade Bag Variant - Unlock by completing Power Out Quest.
data.article: The Bag (Radio Renegade Variant) is a backpack that helps you carry more items during your raids. You can obtain this bag by successfully completing the Power Out quest. Once unlocked, it allows you to bring more resources and supplies back to your Hideout.

data.name: Banana (Backpack Charm)
data.description: Banana backpack charm from Medical Merchandise quest.
data.article: This is a banana-themed backpack charm. Its primary purpose is to serve as an item required for the Medical Merchandise quest. Raiders obtain it as part of their progress within this quest. It has no weight.

data.name: Bandage
data.description: A medical item that gradually restores health over time.
data.article: A Bandage is a medical item used to gradually restore your health over a short period. It helps you recover from damage while out in the field. You can obtain a Bandage by scavenging it from containers or the environment. It can also be crafted at a Medical Lab or a Workbench. If you have the In-Round Crafting skill, you can even craft one during a raid. Additionally, you can purchase one from Lance for 750 coins.

data.name: Barricade Kit
data.description: A deployable cover that can block incoming damage until it breaks.
data.article: The Barricade Kit is a deployable utility item designed to provide temporary cover during raids. Once placed, it creates a wall-like structure that blocks incoming damage, and it can be taken down for reuse. This kit also serves as a surface for placing other defensive tools, such as Laser Traps. Raiders can find it by scavenging or by crafting at the Utility Station. A vendor named Apollo sometimes sells this item for coins.

data.name: Barricade Kit Blueprint
data.description: Lets you craft a Barricade Kit
data.article: The Barricade Kit Blueprint is a blueprint that teaches you how to craft a Barricade Kit at a utility station. It creates a wall-like structure that offers deployable cover, helping to block incoming damage during engagements. These kits can also be dismantled and redeployed. This blueprint is primarily obtained by looting Electrical Style containers across all maps.

data.name: Bastion Cell
data.description: A salvaged component from a Bastion unit. Can be recycled into crafting materials.
data.article: The Bastion Cell is a rare ARC component dropped by a defeated Bastion. It is primarily used to upgrade the Gear Bench, as a turn-in item for the Settled in Full quest and more recently as one of the barter items with Nomadic Traders for account upgrades. Raiders obtain this item by salvaging it from Bastions. Like other components, it can be recycled for valuable resources.

data.name: Battery
data.description: Used to craft medical supplies. Can be recycled into scrap metal.
data.article:
A Battery is a common crafting component used to create various items, fulfill After Rain Comes, and progress through different project stages in your Hideout.

You can find Batteries by searching common containers and interactive panels such as Recording Panels, Oscilloscopes, and Control Consoles across all maps. They are also obtained by salvaging or recycling salvage. Celeste also sells Batteries for coins.

Batteries are used for crafting items at various stations, including the Workbench, Explosives Station, and Gear Bench. You can also recycle them for resources.
